name: Scritti Politti
label: Rough Trade
lede: Green Gartside started out printing his pressing costs and his squat's address on the sleeve, ended up with Miles Davis and Arif Mardin in the credits, and then didn't play a gig for 26 years.

hero.by: Live at the Big Chill, August 2006. Photo: mike de rigueur, Wikimedia Commons

eras.title: A squat in Camden with the address on the sleeve
eras.text: Three art-school friends from Leeds moved to a Camden squat, named the band after Antonio Gramsci and made records that explained how to make records. The politics were Marxist, the sound was scratchy and dubby, and the door was always open.

years.h: The Anarchy tour opens at Leeds Polytechnic, and Gartside takes notes
years.p: The [[Sex Pistols|e5db18cb-4b1f-496d-a308-548b611090d3]] launch the Anarchy tour at the college where Green Gartside studies fine art. He forms a band with his childhood friend Nial Jinks and fellow student Tom Morley.
years.xp:
Gartside and Jinks had known each other since Croesyceiliog Grammar School in Cwmbran, South Wales. Matthew Kay came in as manager and sometime keyboard player.

The first gig went out under another name entirely: the Against, supporting the Leeds punk band SOS.

years.h: Named for Gramsci, spelled like Little Richard
years.p: In Camden Town the band settle on Scritti Politti, after the Italian Marxist Antonio Gramsci. The correct Italian would be Scritti Politici; Gartside bent it toward "Tutti Frutti" because it sounded more rock and roll.

years.src: Reynolds Retro: Scritti Politti retrospective interview · Wikipedia: Scritti Politti
years.h: "Skank Bloc Bologna" comes out on the band's own St. Pancras label
years.p: A nearly six-minute ode to the leftist city of Bologna, self-released, with the squat's address printed for feedback. [[John Peel|e4dec348-ad10-43b6-a2b1-c22aab890675]] plays it.
years.xp:
Simon Reynolds reports that [[Geoff Travis|70437714-3183-4916-947f-e5ba2154d16a]] wanted the single for [[Rough Trade|4f4b0013-1704-4936-a769-e6e8a6e08ff8]], but the Rough Trade collective balked because the song was too long. So the band put it out themselves.

Printing the address brought a steady stream of visitors to the squat. Gartside's list, as Reynolds quotes it: "Disaffected public schoolboys, French hippies, Eurocommunists."

years.src: Wikipedia: Scritti Politti · Reynolds Retro: Scritti Politti retrospective interview
years.h: Rough Trade signs the band, and the sleeves show the receipts
years.p: Travis signs them in 1979, making them labelmates with [[Young Marble Giants|3d113367-769f-4200-9ff8-e19d47def451]]. The sleeves list what everything cost, plus the phone numbers of the pressing plants.
years.xp:
The band went further and wrote a booklet, How To Make A Record, catalogued as SCRIT 3: a guide for anyone who wanted to do what they had just done on their first three singles.

Two EPs followed that year, carrying "Bibbly-O-Tek", "Doubt Beat", "OPEC/Immac" and "Hegemony". Reynolds calls 4 A Sides the early Scritti's best EP.

eras.title: Collapse in Brighton, pop records in Wales
eras.text: A panic attack after a Gang of Four support slot sent Gartside home to South Wales for most of a year. He came back with Aretha Franklin, Chic and the Jacksons in his head and a plan his bandmates didn't much like.

years.big: "Bored shitless with the noise we were making."
years.src: Reynolds Retro: Scritti Politti retrospective interview · Wikipedia: Scritti Politti
years.h: Gartside collapses after a Gang of Four support in Brighton
years.p: He thinks it's a heart attack; it's a panic attack. Nine months recovering in Wales turn him toward pop, and Morley and Jinks aren't keen.
years.xp:
Gartside told Reynolds it was "a monstrous panic attack" and blamed the squat's hardcore lifestyle and the obsessive theorising. His parents insisted he come home to convalesce.

From Wales he wrote the band long notes on why going pop was the right move, then laid down terms, as he told Jamming! in 1982: if they wanted to play on his new songs, great; if not, forget the whole thing.

The pull line is Gartside's own, on why the old sound had to go.

years.h: Robert Wyatt plays keyboards on "The 'Sweetest Girl'"
years.p: The demo lands on the NME's C81 cassette and the New York Times names it a single of the year. The real single takes ten months to come out and stalls at No. 64.
years.xp:
Major labels came calling on the strength of it. Gartside stayed with Rough Trade.

[[Madness|5f58803e-8c4c-478e-8b51-477f38483ede]] covered the song on Mad Not Mad and took it to No. 35 in 1986.

years.src: Wikipedia: Scritti Politti · The Guardian: Pop legend plays first gig for 26 years
years.h: A pop single called "Jacques Derrida"
years.p: "Faithless" reaches No. 56, then the double A-side "Asylums in Jerusalem" / "Jacques Derrida" gets to No. 43. Gartside later befriended the philosopher he'd named a song after.

years.h: Songs to Remember becomes Rough Trade's biggest seller yet
years.p: The debut album reaches No. 12 in the UK and shows off a reggae streak nobody had heard from Gartside before.

years.h: Tom Morley leaves the band
years.p: The drummer who co-founded the group in Leeds departs. Within months the original line-up is gone.

eras.title: New York, Arif Mardin and Miles Davis
eras.text: Gartside signed to Virgin (Warner Bros. in America), moved to New York and rebuilt Scritti Politti around programmer David Gamson and drummer Fred Maher. The records got glossier and the charts got friendlier, and he stopped playing live.

years.src: The Quietus: Green Gartside interviewed · Wikipedia: Scritti Politti
years.h: Gartside signs to Virgin and moves to New York
years.p: Hip-hop and the funk he first heard on Florida radio pull him to the city. He teams up with keyboardist [[David Gamson|30ac0703-9662-42dc-a631-b8b0700fac98]] and ex-Material drummer [[Fred Maher|d1b45986-49cd-4882-946d-58e39764c1f8]].
years.xp:
Gartside told The Quietus about the change: "I became sick. I went back to Caerleon and started listening to my sister's music for the first time." His parents had moved to Florida, and visiting them he heard black radio, the System and Zapp.

Earlier that year he had also sung with Annie Lennox on Eurythmics' "Wrap It Up".

years.src: Wikipedia: Scritti Politti · The Quietus: Green Gartside interviewed
years.h: "Wood Beez (Pray Like Aretha Franklin)" goes Top 10
years.p: The first record from the New York sessions, produced with Aretha Franklin's own producer Arif Mardin, reaches No. 10 in the UK.

yt: The Word Girl, Top of the Pops 1985
years.h: "The Word Girl" climbs to No. 6
years.p: A reggae-styled single, after "Absolute" (No. 17) and "Hypnotize", becomes the band's biggest UK hit.

years.cap: Gartside, David Gamson and Fred Maher, 1985
years.h: Cupid & Psyche 85 goes Top 5 in Britain
years.p: Gamson programs the dense synthesizer counterpoint, Maher drums, Mardin produces three songs. It's the band's most successful album.

years.h: "Perfect Way" flops at home and hits No. 11 in America
years.p: It only reaches No. 48 in the UK. In the US it becomes Scritti's biggest single.

years.cap: UK press kit for Cupid & Psyche 85
years.h: Miles Davis covers "Perfect Way" on Tutu
years.p: The same year Gartside and Gamson write "Love of a Lifetime" for Chaka Khan and the title track of Al Jarreau's L Is for Lover.

years.h: Miles Davis plays trumpet on "Oh Patti"
years.p: Provision adds Roger Troutman and Marcus Miller to the credits and reaches No. 8 in the UK. In the US it stalls at No. 113.
years.xp:
"Oh Patti (Don't Feel Sorry for Loverboy)" reached No. 13. "Best Thing Ever", also on the album, had already turned up on Madonna's Who's That Girl soundtrack in 1987.

The album was nominated for the 1989 Grammy for Best Engineered Recording, Non-Classical.
play: Oh Patti (Don't Feel Sorry for Loverboy)

eras.title: The pub in Usk and a hip-hop record
eras.text: After two cover singles Gartside went back to Wales and largely out of view. When Scritti returned at the end of the decade it was with rappers on the record.

years.h: Shabba Ranks toasts on a Beatles cover
years.p: "She's a Woman", with a William Orbit remix, reaches No. 20: Scritti's last UK Top 20 single. A Gladys Knight cover with Sweetie Irie follows.

years.src: The Guardian: Pop legend plays first gig for 26 years · The Quietus: Green Gartside interviewed
years.h: Gartside leaves for a cottage in Wales
years.p: The Guardian says he was worn out by promoting records on American TV. He told The Quietus he spent years around Usk, in the pubs, listening to hip-hop.
years.xp: The Quietus interview also covers a severe depression after Provision that put him in hospital, in Gartside's own telling.

years.h: Mos Def turns up on Anomie & Bonhomie
years.p: A bearded Gartside makes a hip-hop record with Mos Def and Jimahl among the guests. Critics welcome it back; it reaches No. 33.
years.xp: Virgin's campaign for the album went on to win five pencils at the 2000 D&AD Awards for its graphic design.

eras.title: Double G and the Traitorous 3
eras.text: Back on Rough Trade, now living in Hackney and going to gigs, Gartside tested whether the panic attacks were still there. They weren't, and Scritti Politti became a touring band for the first time since 1980.

years.h: Rough Trade collects the squat years on Early
years.p: The first singles and EPs come back in one place, with liner notes by Gartside.

q: And I didn't, so I guess I'm over it.
years.src: The Guardian: Pop legend plays first gig for 26 years · Wikipedia: Scritti Politti
years.h: Second on the bill at the Windmill in Brixton
years.p: Billed as Double G and the Traitorous 3, Gartside plays his first gig in 26 years in a 100-capacity pub, all new songs, calling it a public rehearsal.
years.xp:
The band included journalist and musician [[Rhodri Marsden|849f9f82-3266-4129-ae9c-ddf7e771b9a2]] on keyboards and Dicky Moore on guitar; the Guardian noted that one member had never played in a band before.

Gartside said afterwards that the show was "a kind of experiment to see if I would get the panic attacks again."

years.src: The Quietus: Green Gartside interviewed · Wikipedia: Scritti Politti
years.h: White Bread Black Beer, made at home in Hackney
years.p: Travis had helped pay for a home studio, and the stripped-down album was recorded there. It's nominated for the Mercury Prize.

years.cap: Rhodri Marsden of the touring band
years.h: Scritti Politti's first North American tour
years.p: Nearly three decades in, the band crosses the Atlantic, after Bestival and Summer Sonic in Japan, and finishes the year at Rough Trade's Christmas party.

years.h: Gamson comes back for two new songs on Absolute
years.p: The singles compilation adds "Day Late and a Dollar Short" and "A Place We Both Belong". Pitchfork names it Best New Reissue.

years.h: Opening for the Manic Street Preachers at Brixton Academy
years.p: Gartside sings lead on the Manics' "Between the Clock and the Bed" from Futurology, and Scritti support three of their shows.

years.h: A solo seven-inch of Anne Briggs songs
years.p: Under his own name on Rough Trade, Gartside covers the folk singer's "Tangled Man" and "Wishing Well".

years.h: Rough Trade buys back the Virgin years
years.p: The label takes over Cupid & Psyche 85, Provision and Anomie & Bonhomie and reissues them on CD and vinyl, with Provision held back until later in the year.
